key_insight: ProxyPose reframes 6-DoF pose tracking as a video-to-video translation problem, allowing pose estimation directly from monocular video. This reduces reliance on extra inputs like 3D models, depth, masks, or handcrafted features.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of tracking object and surface pose from monocular video, especially in difficult cases such as textureless, transparent, reflective, or deformable surfaces where traditional methods often fail.
method: Treat the input video as a source domain and translate it into a proxy representation that encodes pose information.
Use only the video itself as input, avoiding dependence on 3D models, depth maps, object masks, or specialized features.
Learn a video-to-video translation pipeline that outputs pose-relevant signals for 6-DoF tracking across frames.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a simpler and more flexible way to track pose in real-world videos without extra annotations or sensors. It may improve robustness in challenging visual conditions and broaden the usability of pose tracking systems.
